b_rows_sample.anchor: Q1 -- What was actually claimed? ... Q6 -- What is the Gita relationship? The sixth field must explicitly allow: None.
b_rows_sample.statement: Six-question per-step evaluation schema: Q1 what was actually claimed, Q2 what evidence supported it, Q3 domain/DDD concept, Q4 mathematical structure, Q5 invariant, Q6 Gita relationship -- the Gita field must explicitly allow 'None', forbidding manufactured connections.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_0 -- speculation ... E_4 -- runtime/operational evidence. RuntimeEvidence > ImplementationEvidence > Documentation > Assertion.
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidence hierarchy E0<E1<E2<E3<E4: E0 speculation (no evidence), E1 conceptual assertion, E2 documentary evidence, E3 implementation evidence, E4 runtime/operational evidence -- giving RuntimeEvidence > ImplementationEvidence > Documentation > Assertion, meaning stronger evidence for what software does, not necessarily for domain semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim_i from Implemented_i. ... If not, the result could be Intended rather than Confirmed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Claim versus implementation distinction: an architectural claim (e.g. 'KnowledgeOS guarantees provenance') must be tested by Implemented(Provenance)?, yielding Intended rather than Confirmed if unimplemented.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V_i\in\{C,P,I,X,U\} ... V_i=f(Claim_i,Evidence_i,Implementation_i).
b_rows_sample.statement: The five-state verdict vocabulary is retained: C Confirmed, P Partial, I Intended, X Contradicted, U Unknown, formally V_i=f(Claim_i,Evidence_i,Implementation_i).

b_rows_sample.anchor: If we do not have enough evidence: V_i=Unknown. That is a valid architectural result. Unknown>FalseConfidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Why 'Unknown' matters: the audit must resist classifying everything -- insufficient evidence should yield V_i=Unknown as a valid result, with Unknown > FalseConfidence, especially important when auditing a large AI-generated architectural history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_i=(A_i^{soft},A_i^{DDD},A_i^{math},A_i^{gov},A_i^{evidence}). ... This tells us much more than: A_i=0.9.
b_rows_sample.statement: Architecture alignment is explicitly multidimensional: a step can be mathematically coherent yet DDD-incoherent, software-supported yet governance-unsupported, so a single scalar score is inadequate -- instead define a vector A_i=(A_i^soft, A_i^DDD, A_i^math, A_i^gov, A_i^evidence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_i: 1 direct implementation evidence, 0.5 partial evidence, 0 no implementation evidence. But this should remain a diagnostic value -- not a universal metric.
b_rows_sample.statement: Software alignment S_i is a 3-value diagnostic (1 direct evidence, 0.5 partial, 0 none), explicitly kept as a diagnostic value, not a universal metric.

b_rows_sample.anchor: BoundedContext, Aggregate, Entity, ValueObject, DomainEvent, Policy, DomainService, ContextMapping. ... we must not force every mathematical object into an Aggregate.
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD alignment D_i inspects fit against 8 named DDD constructs (BoundedContext, Aggregate, Entity, ValueObject, DomainEvent, Policy, DomainService, ContextMapping), with an explicit warning against forcing every mathematical object into an Aggregate (a category error).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K=document would have poor alignment ... K=(G,\sigma,\theta,\lambda,\pi) could have strong alignment if the software actually demonstrates these dimensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical alignment M_i measures how faithfully a mathematical representation captures the domain claim -- e.g. K=document has poor alignment with the current knowledge-state model, while K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) could have strong alignment only IF the software actually demonstrates these dimensions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MaterialChange\Rightarrow GovernancePath should be tested against the actual governance mechanisms.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance alignment G_i asks whether proposed behavior is consistent with the governance architecture, e.g. testing MaterialChange=>GovernancePath against actual governance mechanisms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H_i as the interpretive relevance, not truth. ... It does not mean: The Gita proves the architecture.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gita alignment H_i is explicitly interpretive relevance, not truth -- H_i=Strong means a meaningful interpretive parallel exists in Chapters 1-4, never that the Gita proves the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G0 -- No meaningful connection ... G3 -- Explicit design influence. ... G3 requires evidence of actual design influence.
b_rows_sample.statement: The Gita four-layer rule (extending/refining the P1/P2/P3 vocabulary): G0 no meaningful connection, G1 analogy (conceptual resemblance), G2 interpretive principle (philosophical lens), G3 explicit design influence (architecture consciously designed using the interpretation) -- G3 explicitly requires historical evidence of actual design influence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Some engineering principles independently emerge from software architecture, mathematics, epistemology and governance; Chapters 1-4 of the Gita provide an additional interpretive lens for understanding selected principles. That is much more defensible.
b_rows_sample.statement: The G0-G3 discipline is justified as protecting the book against retroactively claiming every KnowledgeOS concept originated from the Gita, favoring the defensible framing that engineering principles independently emerge while the Gita provides an additional interpretive lens.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step | Original claim | Evidence | Software | DDD | Mathematics | Governance | Gita | Verdict. This becomes the canonical audit artifact.
b_rows_sample.statement: The canonical alignment audit table for all 182 steps: columns Step, Original claim, Evidence, Software, DDD, Mathematics, Governance, Gita (G0-G3), Verdict -- designated the canonical audit artifact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_{ij}=1 if Step i and Step j contain materially conflicting claims. ... {Temporal, Contextual, Terminological, Architectural, Mathematical, Implementation, Governance}.
b_rows_sample.statement: A separate contradiction register defines C_ij=1 when steps i and j materially conflict, classified into 7 contradiction types (Temporal, Contextual, Terminological, Architectural, Mathematical, Implementation, Governance) -- apparent contradiction does not necessarily mean error.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Term(t)=\{Meaning_1,\ldots,Meaning_n\}. ... Meaning(t,C_A)\stackrel{?}{=}Meaning(t,C_B). If not: ContextualPolysemy must be explicitly recorded.
b_rows_sample.statement: Terminology drift is formalized: Term(t) may map to multiple meanings across steps, tested via Meaning(t,C_A) =? Meaning(t,C_B); if unequal, ContextualPolysemy must be explicitly recorded as a direct DDD concern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K means knowledge item in one step and knowledge state in another, then K_1\neq K_2. ... a notation dictionary. K\rightarrow KnowledgeState, k\rightarrow KnowledgeItem, G\rightarrow KnowledgeGraph, ... P\rightarrow Policy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical notation drift mirrors terminology drift (e.g. K meaning 'knowledge item' in one step vs 'knowledge state' in another gives K1!=K2); a provisional notation dictionary is proposed (K->KnowledgeState, k->KnowledgeItem, G->KnowledgeGraph, C->Context, T->Transformation, E->Evidence, A->Authority, P->Policy), pending confirmation by the Steps 1-182 audit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision\leftarrow Evidence\leftarrow Observation/Requirement. ... Why do we believe our architecture? This is different from: Why does the software behave this way? Both are needed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Architecture decision provenance is a second-order provenance structure (Decision<-Evidence<-Observation/Requirement) answering 'why do we believe our architecture', explicitly distinct from and complementary to 'why does the software behave this way'.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 11 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #3 — The evidence-strength scale is recalibrated between Step 210 and Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.30 defines E_1=documentation, E_2=manual inspection, E_3=automated test, E_4=property-based test, E_5=formal verification. Step 212 Section 212.6 defines E_0=No evidence, E_1=Claim/documentation, E_2=Static implementation evidence, E_3=Executable test evidence, E_4=Runtime/production evidence, E_5=Formal verification. E_2, E_3 and E_4 disagree between the two files (only E_5 agrees), so a claim 'has E_4 evidence' means a property-based test under Step 210 and production observation under Step 212 -- entirely different assurance. Aggravating factor: Step 212's calibration silently matches the uncited Step 109's (E2=implementation, E4=runtime), so Step 212 restores an earlier convention without knowing it. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #4 — E_1 bound twice inside Step 210 itself
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P (evidence items entailing propositions); Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (an ordinal assurance rung). Same symbol, same document, incompatible types, undisambiguated. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #5 — Evidence/Test ordering reversed between Step 210's own boxed conclusion and Step 211's boxed conclusion
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.40 boxes Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance; Step 211 Section 211.2 boxes I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence -- directly conflicting orderings, both boxed as conclusions in consecutive files. Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple and Step 209's tail agenda both side with Step 211's ordering, so Step 210's boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own boxed tuple. Severity MEDIUM; the direction matters since Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test while Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #6 — min over assurance vs. the prohibition on scalarization, both boxed in Step 211
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 Section 211.6 states Assurance(I_global)<=min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}; Step 211 Section 211.17 boxes 'Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization.' min over a set requires a total order on the codomain, but Section 211.9 makes assurance a 6-vector (only partially ordered), so evaluating min requires exactly the scalarization Section 211.17 forbids -- the two boxed positions of one file are mutually exclusive. Aggravated by Section 211.4's ordinal-only assurance-adjacent quantities and by Section 211.17's own use of cardinal values A_s=1, A_p=0, 0.83. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #7 — Step 212 builds ownership diagnostics and deletes the ownership data needed to run them
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 boxes 'Ownerless Invariants' as a finding to explicitly search for (I exists but Owner(I)=empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4's register reprints all fifteen invariants with the Owner column removed (columns reduced to ID|Property|Target), and no search for ownerless invariants is performed anywhere in the file. Step 210's deleted Owner column contained exactly the data Sections 212.15/212.16 are designed to interrogate: 7 of 15 rows owned by a layer or pattern (effectively ownerless), 5 of 15 slash-shared. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #8 — F/D/P/U mandated in Step 213, applied zero times across Steps 213-215
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 213 Section 213.26 mandates that every important statement during reconstruction carry an [F]/[D]/[P]/[U] label ('our editorial control system'). A machine count of applied labels in Steps 213, 214, and 215 finds 4, 0, 0 respectively, and all four occurrences in 213 are the legend itself. Zero of the hundreds of statements in the three files that mandate the labels carry one, even though Section 213.26 explicitly scopes the requirement to these reconstruction documents themselves. Severity HIGH; this is a performative contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #9 — Step 214's self-assessment table violates Step 214's own boxed evidentiary rule eight lines later
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 214 Section 214.32 boxes 'no architectural claim should be stronger than the evidence supporting it.' Step 214 Section 214.33's final row states 'Risk of overclaiming | Explicitly controlled' -- a claim about the corpus's own overclaiming risk with zero supporting evidence, in a table that also self-awards 'Very strong' on five dimensions in a file containing no evidence at all. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #10 — Three incompatible ledger arities inside Step 214
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 214 Section 214.1 boxes a 10-tuple EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status); Section 214.6 gives a 15-field schema table; the Section 214 tail (line 1095) gives an 8-column matrix header whose columns barely overlap the 10-tuple's. Three incompatible schemas for 'the Evidence Ledger' in one file, with no reconciliation and no statement of which is normative. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #11 — Step 215 prohibits new formulas and mints three (four) in the same file
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 215 Section 215.30 prohibits 'creat[ing] more theoretical formulas merely because we can,' yet the same file mints R(S_i)=(O_i,L_i,A_i,V_i,U_i) (215.1), Convergence(I)=NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) (215.7), the boxed SemanticIntegrity∝DistinctionPreservation (215.10), and the boxed B=Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection) (215.32) -- four new formal objects, none computed. Severity MEDIUM; aggravated because the proportionality is not merely new but ill-typed, and Synthesize is never specified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #12 — Step 215 exempts itself and its seven predecessors from its own discipline
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 215 Section 215.31 (Phase 1) targets S_1...S_182 -> EvidenceLedger, goal 'understand what actually happened'; the same file's closing paragraph defers 'what we previously called Step 183 onward' to a later decision about renaming or absorption. Steps 183-215 include all eight in-scope files of this verification, so the reconstruction discipline is scoped to exclude the very documents that mandate it -- compounded by Contradiction #8 (zero labels applied). Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #13 — The scope of the derivation phase disagrees between Step 212 and Step 215
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.5 states 'Steps 1-211 have largely been derivation'; Step 215 Section 215.31 and five other occurrences scope the reconstruction to S_1...S_182. The corpus states the derivation ran to 211 while scoping reconstruction to 182; the 29-step remainder is never reconciled, and 182 is never justified anywhere. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #16 — Invariants modeled as a dependency graph and as a flat conjunction, consecutively, within Step 209
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.31 states that some invariants depend on others (HistoricalTraceability depends on Identity+Versioning+Provenance), illustrated with a 24-line ASCII dependency graph. Step 209 Section 209.32 then composes all invariants as a flat, order-free conjunction I_global=AND_{i=1}^n I_i. A conjunction cannot express dependency; the two sections model the same invariant set with incompatible structures, consecutively. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Total: 16 contradictions. Six are internal to a single file; ten are cross-file within the band.
a_rows_sample.statement: Summary tally of Part 6's contradiction catalogue across Steps 208-215: 16 contradictions total, of which six are internal to a single file (#4, #6, #9, #10, #11, #16) and ten are cross-file within the band (#1, #2, #3, #5, #7, #8, #12, #13, #14, #15).

a_rows_sample.anchor: O-15 — 16 contradictions, six internal to a single file.
a_rows_sample.statement: Highest severity: #1 (Knowledge as owner, forbidden two files earlier), #2 (provenance equation excludes the authority 209.4 requires; vacuous-or-self-refuting), #3 (evidence scale recalibrated), #6 (min vs no-scalarization, both boxed in one file), #7 (ownership diagnostics built, ownership data deleted), #8 (F/D/P/U mandated, never applied), #12 (self-exemption).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status(I) in {Implemented, Partial, Specified, Missing, Unknown} ... Unknown != Missing ... Unknown != Implemented
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-value implementation-status classification for every architectural property (Implemented/Partial/Specified/Missing/Unknown), with boxed guardrails Unknown!=Missing and Unknown!=Implemented -- the distinction between Missing and Unknown is called critical.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We derive a good architectural principle and gradually begin speaking about it as though the existing system already implements it. That would be architectural hallucination ... Derived Architecture != Current Architecture
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the risk of 'architectural hallucination' -- gradually treating a derived architectural principle as though the existing system already implements it -- and sets a strict boundary Derived Architecture != Current Architecture, requiring the current architecture to be established from evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G_i=(I_i,Status,Owner,Mechanism,Evidence,Confidence,Gap)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a per-invariant evidence record G_i=(Invariant,Status,Owner,Mechanism,Evidence,Confidence,Gap) as the unit of the architecture audit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I1 Identity ≠ State ... I15 No silent semantic strengthening ... none of these should yet be marked 'Implemented' merely because we derived them
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists a first 15-item theoretical assurance register (I1-I15: Identity!=State, historical version preservation, provenance preservation, epistemic status preservation, Unknown!=False, uncertainty preservation, model-version integrity, Inference!=Authority, Decision!=Execution, Execution!=Outcome, contradiction preservation, temporal validity, legal state transitions, pre/postconditions, no silent semantic strengthening), explicitly marked as targets not yet verified as implemented.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_0=No evidence ... E_5=Formal verification
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-level evidence-quality hierarchy E0 (no evidence) through E5 (formal verification), via E1 claim/documentation, E2 static implementation evidence, E3 executable test evidence, E4 runtime/production evidence, worked through a provenance example progressing from documentation claim to automated evidence-chain test to production lineage recording.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence(I) != EvidenceLevel(I)
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates evidence strength from confidence: strong (E2) evidence from inspecting only one module may still leave confidence in system-wide enforcement low; Confidence(I) != EvidenceLevel(I).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The architecture is 82% compliant ... unless we have first defined ... population ... weighting ... independence ... evidence quality ... confidence model ... treatment of critical properties
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against stating an unsupported compliance percentage (e.g. '82% compliant') without first defining the requirement population, weighting, independence, evidence quality, confidence model and treatment of critical properties; recommends a qualitative CriticalGap measure instead.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G1 — Semantic gap ... G5 — Assurance gap ... These gaps can coexist
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five coexisting gap classes: G1 Semantic (software loses domain meaning), G2 Governance (authority/responsibility ambiguous), G3 Temporal (historical state not reconstructable), G4 Epistemic (evidence/uncertainty/assumptions lost), G5 Assurance (behavior may be correct but insufficiently evidenced).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implementation = Present but Assurance = Weak. This is not necessarily an implementation gap. It is an: Assurance Gap
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example distinguishing implementation presence from assurance: modelVersion correctly stored (Implementation=Present) but with no automated test proving it survives the workflow (Assurance=Weak) is classified specifically as an Assurance Gap, not an implementation gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ArchitectureGap != ImplementationGap != VerificationGap
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Architecture gap (design itself lacks the mechanism), Implementation gap (mechanism specified but code does not implement it correctly), and Verification gap (implementation appears correct but evidence is insufficient) as three non-identical gap types.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TechnicalCapability=Present while GovernanceCapability=Missing ... Ownerless Invariants ... Shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a governance gap pattern where a technical mechanism (AI->Assessment->Approval) works but nobody has defined who is authorized to approve, so TechnicalCapability=Present while GovernanceCapability=Missing; introduces the 'ownerless invariant' search (Owner(I)=empty set, dangerous because nobody maintains it) and its converse, the 'shared ownership' problem, where undivided shared responsibility (Owner(I)={A,B,C}) risks each team assuming another enforces the invariant -- boxed as 'shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) ... Loss(C)={p | p in CriticalProperties and p absent after transformation}
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-loss function for a context-to-context contract L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C), refined to Loss(C) as the set of critical properties absent after transformation; worked example: an Assessment=(score,uncertainty,modelVersion,evidenceRef) contract sending only {score} loses uncertainty/modelVersion/evidenceRef, a Critical Semantic Gap if downstream governance requires them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ΔT=T_target △ T_actual where △ denotes symmetric difference ... Unauthorized State Transition Path
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconstructing actual state-machine transitions T_actual from implementation and comparing to target transitions T_target via symmetric difference DeltaT = T_target triangle T_actual as a state-transition gap measure; a transition present in T_actual but absent from T_target is an Unauthorized State Transition Path warranting high priority when governance consequences exist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t) ... Reproducibility ... Replayability ... A system may be replayable without being perfectly reproducible
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines historical replay Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t), noting exact replay (Replay(A,t)=A_t) may be impossible when external conditions change, in which case the system should preserve enough provenance to explain why; distinguishes Reproducibility (can we regenerate the same result, F(X,M)=Y again) from Replayability (can we reconstruct what happened and why), noting a system may be replayable without being reproducible (e.g. a now-defunct external service).

b_rows_sample.anchor: A new state does not necessarily know the old state ... CurrentState + HistoricalProvenance ... History must be preservable, not necessarily embedded in every current state
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a technically disciplined reading of an earlier 'Chapter 4' observation ('a new state does not necessarily know the old state'): rejects CurrentState=History, proposing instead CurrentState+HistoricalProvenance as sufficient for reconstructing relevant prior meaning; boxed principle: history must be preservable, not necessarily embedded in every current state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prediction -> AutomaticAuthority ... CurrentState -> AssumeCompleteHistory ... Unknown -> False ... Execution -> AssumeSuccess ... Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions
b_rows_sample.statement: States a negative-space design principle: a mature architecture must specify ForbiddenPaths as well as AllowedPaths (Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions), and lists four named forbidden implicit transitions to guard against: Prediction->AutomaticAuthority, CurrentState->AssumeCompleteHistory, Unknown->False, Execution->AssumeSuccess.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assessment -/-> Authority ... The X is important. It represents a path that the architecture must prevent
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Step 211 Architecture Assurance Graph with an explicit forbidden-path marker: Evidence->Assessment->Governance->Decision->Authorized Action->Execution->Outcome, with an explicit forbidden edge Assessment-/->Authority that the architecture must prevent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G-01 Identity ... G-15 History ... This is the audit instrument
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a 15-item provisional gap register (G-01 through G-15) as concrete audit questions (identity/state separation, historical reconstructability, provenance traceability, uncertainty preservation across boundaries, model/version provenance, inference-to-authority escalation, decision/execution separation, execution/outcome separation, illegal transition blocking, contract semantic loss, contradiction coexistence, unknown-vs-false distinguishability, automatic critical-invariant testing, single accountable ownership, prior semantic context reconstruction).

b_rows_sample.anchor: No evidence => Unknown. Not: No evidence => Missing. And certainly not: No evidence => Implemented
b_rows_sample.statement: States the methodological rule of Step 212 as most important: the gap register's rows must not be populated by imagination but from actual KnowledgeOS artifacts, with the default for absence of evidence being No evidence=>Unknown, explicitly not =>Missing and certainly not =>Implemented.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### Architectural reasoning PASS ... Gītā Chapters 1–4 COHERENT
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 verdict: architectural reasoning, DDD, mathematics, statistics, and AI dimensions each rated PASS; Gita chapters 1-4 rated COHERENT (continuing to generate architectural questions without being presented as technical proof).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 4 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: What happened? ... What remained unknown? ... R(S_i)=(O_i,L_i,A_i,V_i,U_i)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-question per-step reconstruction record R(S_i)=(Observation,Learning,Architecture,Verification,Unknown) to be applied to each of Steps 1-182, explicitly changing mode from generating new theory to reconstructing the evidentiary basis of existing theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: StepCount ≠ KnowledgeCount ... exploratory; repetitive; corrective; validation; implementation; philosophical; mathematical; editorial; prompt-engineering; synthesis
a_rows_sample.statement: States that a conversational 'step' is not necessarily an architectural contribution (some are exploratory, repetitive, corrective, editorial, etc.), so StepCount != KnowledgeCount, requiring the reconstruction to discover the actual knowledge-bearing events rather than treat all 182 steps as equal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OBS Observation ... UNK Insufficient evidence ... A single step can have more than one tag internally
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a 14-code step-type classification (OBS/EXP/MAT/DDD/ARC/GOV/AI/VER/FAIL/DEC/PHI/SYN/REP/UNK) allowing multiple tags per step, crossed with the F/D/P/U epistemic-status axis (Type x EpistemicStatus) so e.g. 'ARC+D' denotes an architectural derivation rather than an observed fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Which architectural principles appear independently more than once? ... Convergence(I) = NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) ... We should not immediately turn this into a numerical quality score
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a convergence test: if the same architectural principle emerges from multiple unrelated observations (P_1, P_7, P_31 all pointing to invariant I), that repeated independent emergence is treated as strong evidence the principle is fundamental, formalized as Convergence(I)=NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) but explicitly not reduced to a numerical quality score.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity≠State ... Knowledge≠Authority ... Unknown≠False ... CurrentState≠History ... Generation≠Validation ... Validation≠Authorization ... Claim→Evidence ... Context_A≠Context_B ... These are candidate principles, not yet declared final conclusions
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists ten candidate recurring architectural distinctions to be tested against the actual Steps-1-182 evidence rather than accepted by default (Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Authority, Decision!=Execution, Execution!=Outcome, Unknown!=False, CurrentState!=History, Generation!=Validation, Validation!=Authorization, Claim->Evidence, Context_A!=Context_B), explicitly labelled candidates pending evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: They are all forms of: A ≠ B where software engineering frequently makes the mistake: A ≈ B ... restoring distinctions that had been collapsed
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a deeper common structure across the recurring principles: each is an instance of A!=B guarding against a common engineering mistake of collapsing A~=B (Identity~=State, Prediction~=Truth, Knowledge~=Authority, Execution~=Outcome), proposing this pattern-of-restoring-collapsed-distinctions as possibly one of the deepest architectural themes in the entire book.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Robust knowledge-centric software depends on preserving distinctions that carry semantic, temporal, epistemic or governance meaning ... SemanticIntegrity ∝ DistinctionPreservation ... a hypothesis, not a proven theorem
a_rows_sample.statement: States the 'distinction preservation' hypothesis (robust knowledge-centric software depends on preserving semantically/temporally/epistemically/governance-meaningful distinctions), formalized as SemanticIntegrity proportional-to DistinctionPreservation, explicitly labelled a hypothesis to be tested against the Steps-1-182 evidence rather than a proven theorem; connects this across DDD (Entity!=ValueObject), mathematics (x!=y), statistics (Observed!=Inferred, Correlation!=Causation), governance (Capability!=Authority) and AI engineering (Generation!=Verification) as convergent instances of one meta-principle: do not collapse distinctions that matter.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Krishna ~ Perspective possessing continuity across changing manifestations ... What would a software system need if it were required to preserve continuity across changing states? ... Versioning, Provenance, History, Lineage, Context
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a careful literary (not architectural) interpretation of Krishna as 'a perspective possessing continuity across changing manifestations', translating this into the engineering question of what a system needs to preserve continuity across changing states (versioning, provenance, history, lineage, context), explicitly warning against the trivializing claim 'Krishna is the system's memory'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Philosophical Analogy ≠ Technical Proof ... Outcome A ... retrospective analogy ... Outcome B ... repeatedly influenced ... Outcome C ... independently emerged technically and philosophically ... the most interesting result
a_rows_sample.statement: States three possible historical outcomes for the Gita lens's actual role to be determined by the reconstruction rather than assumed: (A) it was purely a retrospective analogy applied after the fact, (B) it repeatedly and genuinely influenced engineering questions during development, (C) the same principles independently emerged both technically and philosophically -- rated the most interesting possible result, expressible as EngineeringObservation<->PhilosophicalReflection without either proving the other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose a technical invariant existed before the corresponding Gītā reflection ... TechnicalDiscovery -> PhilosophicalRecognition ... those are different histories. The Evidence Ledger will tell us which actually occurred
a_rows_sample.statement: States that chronology determines which of two different intellectual histories occurred (technical discovery preceding philosophical recognition, or vice versa) and that only the actual Evidence Ledger -- not narrative preference -- can establish which; reframes Step 215's most important task as determining 'when did the idea enter the reasoning', not merely what was concluded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 182 Steps -> 43 SignificantEvents -> 17 CoreInsights -> 8 ArchitecturalPrinciples -> 4 MajorThemes. The exact numbers are unknown
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a compression pipeline reducing 182 raw steps to a small number of significant events, core insights, architectural principles, and major themes (illustrative counts only, explicitly not fixed), arguing the book should present the intellectual structure hidden inside the steps rather than the 182 steps themselves; proposes an intermediate 5-epoch structure (Problem Recognition -> Experimentation -> DDD/Domain Modeling -> Mathematical/Epistemic Formalization -> KnowledgeOS/AI-Engineering Architecture) explicitly not to be frozen before the evidence determines it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture_observed ... Architecture_designed ... Architecture_implemented ... Architecture_proposed ... Observed ≠ Intended ≠ Implemented ≠ Target
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns that the single word 'architecture' conflates at least four distinct referents (observed, intended, implemented, target/proposed) that may differ from each other, proposing Observed!=Intended!=Implemented!=Target as a central reconstruction rule; separately notes that linguistic markers in generated text ('should' signals P, 'the code contains' signals F if verified, 'therefore requires' signals D) can help automatically classify epistemic status at scale.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step Source Artifact Date/Sequence Primary Topic Type Observation Fact Hypothesis Experiment Result Derived Insight Decision Rejected Alternative Architectural Principle Invariant Evidence Gita Connection Status [F/D/P/U] Confidence Open Question
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the Step 215 Artifact: a 19-column Master Reconstruction Matrix schema intended as the master source for eventual book-writing, including a dedicated 'Gita Connection' column and 'Rejected Alternative' column.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not: rewrite the book; freeze the chapter structure; invent missing evidence; merge competing concepts; eliminate contradictions; assume implementation ... Reconstruct. Analyze. Synthesize. Write.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists nine things not to do before reconstruction is complete (rewrite the book, freeze chapter structure, invent missing evidence, merge competing concepts, eliminate contradictions, assume implementation, over-architect philosophical analogies, assign arbitrary percentages, create formulas for their own sake), sequencing the correct order as Reconstruct -> Analyze -> Synthesize -> Write.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 1 — Archaeology ... Phase 2 — Separation of Concerns ... Phase 3 — Synthesis ... This is the correct point at which Claude should eventually begin chapter-by-chapter writing. Not before
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a three-phase book-production architecture: Phase 1 Archaeology (S1..S182 -> Evidence Ledger, understand what happened), Phase 2 Separation of Concerns (separate Facts from Derivations from Proposals from PhilosophicalInterpretations, preventing conceptual contamination), Phase 3 Synthesis (Evidence->Patterns->Principles->Architecture->Book), stating chapter-by-chapter writing is correct only after all three phases, not before.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B = Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection) ... ClaimStrength ≤ EvidenceStrength ... PhilosophicalReflection ≠ TechnicalEvidence ... CurrentArchitecture ≠ TargetArchitecture
a_rows_sample.statement: States the final synthesis equation for the whole book-generation process, B=Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection), subject to three boxed constraints (ClaimStrength<=EvidenceStrength, PhilosophicalReflection!=TechnicalEvidence, CurrentArchitecture!=TargetArchitecture), explicitly framed as protecting the book against retrospective rewriting, overclaiming, and confusing philosophy with engineering proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: It should be the actual execution of the reconstruction ... I should not fabricate their contents from the current conversation ... Once they are available here, we can process them in batches
a_rows_sample.statement: Previews Step 216: not another theoretical step but the actual execution of the reconstruction, explicitly refusing to fabricate the contents of Steps 1-182 from memory/conversation and requiring the real historical artifacts to be brought in and processed in batches, after which Step 183 onward may need renaming or absorption into the synthesis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

a_rows_sample.anchor: IT SPECIFIES A METHOD. It reconstructs nothing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Exhaustive machine count of every step-index token in Step 215 ('Reconstruct Steps 1-182'): of the 182 steps, only 6 are individually named (1, 2, 3, 73, 91, 182), 0 are quoted, 0 are given any content, 0 are given a substantive verdict, and 176 never appear at all. The file's only data matrix (Section 215.5) has 40 cells (8 columns x 5 rows): 28 are the placeholder '...' and 12 are filled, all with step index/type-tag/status-tag -- zero cells contain information about any of the 182 steps. Step 215 itself concedes 'the exact contents must come from the actual saved artifacts, not memory or invention,' and names its own future deliverable, the 'Step 215 Artifact — Master Reconstruction Matrix,' as not yet produced.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the two live step indices used as notation examples do not match the real corpus steps they name
a_rows_sample.statement: Verifiable error in Step 215's notation examples: Step 91's real corpus file is titled 'Formal Specification and Refinement', but Step 215 tags it 'EXP + F' (an experimentally established fact); under Step 215's own taxonomy (Section 215.3) a formal-specification step should be tagged MAT or VER, not EXP. Step 73 ('Identity, Trust and Cryptographic Provenance') tagged 'ARC + D' is defensible and not called an error. The Step 91 mismatch's status is ambiguous as to intent (possibly pure notation demonstration) but unambiguous as to fact: the tag does not describe the step it names. Not silently repaired.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Artifacts -> Evidence -> Facts -> Interpretations -> Patterns -> Principles -> Architecture -> Book ... We must not skip Artifacts->Evidence by jumping directly to Artifacts->Architecture
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the full reconstruction pipeline (Artifacts->Evidence->Facts->Interpretations->Patterns->Principles->Architecture->Book) as five internal epistemic layers (Source S, Evidence E(S), Interpretation I(E), Architecture A(I), Synthesis T(A)) with an explicit rule against skipping the Artifacts->Evidence step by jumping straight to Architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A later theory must not be used to rewrite an earlier source ... T ↛ S ... A ↛ E unless we are explicitly performing a verification
b_rows_sample.statement: States a one-directional-flow rule (a later theory T must not rewrite an earlier source S, and Architecture must not rewrite Evidence, except when explicitly performing Verification) and distinguishes Discovery (Evidence->Architecture, asking what architecture emerged) from Verification (Architecture->Evidence, asking does the evidence support this claim) as two legitimate but different directions that must be labelled separately.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claude must actively search for: EvidenceFor(I) and EvidenceAgainst(I) ... Audit(I) = Support(I) + Contradiction(I)
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against confirmation bias in the reconstruction (unconsciously searching artifacts only for evidence supporting a favored idea) and requires an explicit audit function Audit(I)=Support(I)+Contradiction(I) searching for both.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the reconstruction should initially preserve: {A, ¬A} ... A(t_1)=True and A(t_2)=False. Therefore every major claim should ... be interpreted as: Claim(Context,Time)
b_rows_sample.statement: States that contradictory artifact claims should initially be preserved as a set {A, not-A} pending investigation of context/time/version/scope/definition, and that apparent contradictions across time may resolve into versioned truth (A(t1)=True, A(t2)=False without either being 'wrong'), so major claims should be interpreted as Claim(Context,Time).

b_rows_sample.anchor: P1 — Historical influence ... P2 — Conceptual correspondence ... P3 — Retrospective interpretation ... These must not be conflated
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a three-label classification (P1 Historical influence: evidence shows the philosophical idea influenced engineering reasoning; P2 Conceptual correspondence: independent structural similarity; P3 Retrospective interpretation: the connection was recognized only later) for every Gita-to-architecture connection recorded in the reconstruction, operationalizing step 215's three-outcome hypothesis into a per-instance tag; adds a seven-field philosophical evidence ledger schema (Chapter, Concept, Technical analogue, Relationship P1/P2/P3, Historical evidence, Architectural consequence, Caveat).

b_rows_sample.anchor: M ∈ {Definition, Identity, Derivation, Model, Approximation, Heuristic} ... A formula appearing mathematically elegant does not automatically make it a theorem
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires classifying every mathematical formula encountered in the reconstruction into one of six categories (Definition/Identity/Derivation/Model/Approximation/Heuristic), illustrated by contrasting a conceptual model (Gap=Target-Current) against a precise set-theoretic construction (a symmetric-difference formula), with the boxed principle Mathematical notation != mathematical proof; separately requires every statistical claim to preserve Population/Sample/Assumption/Method/Uncertainty, warning ObservedFrequency does not automatically imply UnderlyingProbability without an inference model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ConceptualArchitecture ... LogicalArchitecture ... PhysicalArchitecture ... Implementation ... Each layer needs its own evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes four architecture layers (Conceptual/Logical/Physical/Implementation) each requiring its own separate evidence, with a worked example (Evidence-must-be-traceable -> Evidence Registry -> Repository/service/database -> actual classes/tables/APIs/tests); defines an implementation-truth test (for any claimed capability ask Where/How/How-was-it-verified, defaulting to Status=Unknown if unanswerable) and a target-architecture test (for any proposed capability ask Why/Which-invariant/Which-evidence/What-tradeoff, otherwise it is architectural preference not justified design).

b_rows_sample.anchor: AD=(P,E,C,A,R,T) ... stronger than: 'We chose X because it is better'
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-field Architecture Decision record AD=(Problem,Evidence,Constraints,Alternatives,Rationale,Tradeoffs), explicitly stronger than an unsupported preference statement; requires trade-offs to be recorded explicitly (e.g. Reliability at the expense of Complexity, Auditability at the expense of Storage, Determinism at the expense of Flexibility) since no universally optimal architecture exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A* = argmax_A U(A) subject to Constraints(A) ... U is multi-dimensional ... there may be no unique optimum ... Pareto frontier
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes architecture selection as multi-objective optimization A*=argmax U(A) subject to Constraints(A), where U is multi-dimensional (Correctness, Traceability, Governability, Maintainability, Performance, Cost, Flexibility) and therefore has no unique optimum in general; proposes a Pareto-frontier framing where multiple architectures may be mutually non-dominated, with final choice depending on governance priorities -- called more honest than declaring one architecture universally superior.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeIntegrity + EngineeringVelocity + Governance + Evidence + AI Assurance ... B = Time+Money+Complexity+HumanAttention ... AssuranceInvestment must be proportional to Risk × Consequence
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS optimizes a broad, potentially-conflicting objective set (KnowledgeIntegrity, EngineeringVelocity, Governance, Evidence, AI Assurance) rather than mere performance; introduces an 'assurance budget' B=Time+Money+Complexity+HumanAttention that assurance mechanisms consume, requiring AssuranceInvestment to scale proportionally to Risk times Consequence rather than attempting maximal assurance everywhere.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Priority(I_i) = Risk(I_i) × Impact(I_i) ... Criticality(I) in {Low, Medium, High, Critical} ... Critical -> AutomatedTest + StaticCheck + RuntimeEvidence + GovernanceReview
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines invariant priority as Risk times Impact and a four-level criticality classification, scaling verification mechanism strength accordingly (a Critical invariant requires automated test plus static check plus runtime evidence plus governance review, a low-impact one only a unit test), avoiding an architecture that treats every property equally; connects this to the deterministic-assurance boundary: AI generates candidates, deterministic mechanisms constrain them, and human/governed decision remains in the loop for risk-scaled workflows (avoiding both unchecked AI and fully manual human review).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence precedes interpretation ... Interpretation precedes architectural synthesis ... AI interpretation is not primary evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States Step 216's consolidated seven-principle 'reconstruction constitution': evidence precedes interpretation; interpretation precedes architectural synthesis; architectural claims retain provenance; contradictions are preserved before resolution; historical states are not overwritten by current understanding; philosophical analogy is not technical evidence; AI interpretation is not primary evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Pass 1 — Extraction ... Pass 8 — Book synthesis ... Only now produce
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Step 217's eight-pass execution protocol for actually reconstructing the saved Steps 1-182 material: Extraction (read all, do not synthesize), Separation (classify F/D/P/U and by discipline), Contradiction detection (find and do not auto-resolve conflicting claims), Pattern discovery, Invariant extraction (promote a pattern to invariant only via evidence+reasoning), Architecture mapping (Invariant->BoundedContext->Component->Mechanism->Test), Historical synthesis (reconstruct t1->t2->...->tn), and only then Book synthesis (Chapter->Section->Argument->Evidence->Architecture).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claude must stop synthesis whenever the evidence is insufficient. It should write: UNKNOWN — insufficient evidence ... BookClaim -> ArchitecturalPrinciple -> Derivation -> Evidence -> SourceArtifact
b_rows_sample.statement: States Step 217's crucial stopping rule (write 'UNKNOWN -- insufficient evidence' rather than inventing an explanation) and its final quality criterion: every major book statement must be traceable backward (BookClaim->ArchitecturalPrinciple->Derivation->Evidence->SourceArtifact) and forward (Invariant->Implementation->Verification->Evidence), producing what is called an auditable intellectual and engineering history rather than a conventional architecture document; closes by reframing the entire project's guiding question from 'what architecture should we invent next' to 'what has the evidence already taught us, and where does it still say we do not know'.

lineage_claims_b_to_a.quote: We should now formalize how Gītā material enters the reconstruction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 279 does not create new theory. It attempts to execute the existing theory and records exactly where formal specification survives contact with computation. ... $$\boxed{\text{Specification} \rightarrow \text{Implementation} \rightarrow \text{Execution} \rightarrow \text{Evidence}}$$ and not: $$\text{Specification} \rightarrow \text{Assumed correctness}.$$
a_rows_sample.statement: States the governing methodological rule for Step 279: the pipeline must be Specification -> Implementation -> Execution -> Evidence, explicitly rejecting Specification -> Assumed correctness. The implementation prompt prohibits silently repairing failures or treating formal specification as empirical fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 279 covers only the Policy and Authority governance layer. It MUST NOT redesign: K; Sigma; the transformation theory; the previously established epistemic model; bounded-context boundaries.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly scopes Step 279 to the Policy/Authority governance layer only, prohibiting redesign of K, Sigma, transformation theory, the epistemic model, or bounded-context boundaries -- treating those as fixed inputs.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$PID = Hash(content,rules,parameters,authority,validity)$$ ... A policy version is immutable after activation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Implements Step 278's content-addressed policy identity: PID = Hash(content, rules, parameters, authority, validity), with a policy version treated as immutable after activation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The implementation MUST NOT: $$Unknown \rightarrow Deny$$ or: $$Conditional \rightarrow Permit.$$ These are explicitly prohibited fallback behaviours.
a_rows_sample.statement: Prohibits two specific unsafe fallback behaviours in the authorization evaluator: an Unknown verdict must never be silently converted to Deny, and a Conditional verdict must never be silently converted to Permit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$Scale \in \{Nominal, Ordinal, Interval, Ratio\}.$$ No arithmetic operation may be applied merely because a value is numerically encoded. In particular: $$Ordinal \not\Rightarrow Interval.$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates explicit measurement-scale typing (Nominal/Ordinal/Interval/Ratio) for any quantitative policy rule, forbidding arithmetic operations merely because a value is numerically encoded, and specifically forbidding treating an ordinal scale as if it were interval-scaled.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$Calibration = (Model, ValidationData, CalibrationMetric)$$ and: $$CalibrationVerified \iff CalibrationMetric \le Threshold.$$ This prevents an asserted probability from being treated as automatically trustworthy merely because a model produced it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires any probabilistic policy criterion (P(theta>c|X)>=q) to reference an explicit statistical model with a calibration triple (Model, ValidationData, CalibrationMetric) and threshold comparison, preventing an asserted probability from being automatically trusted merely because some model produced it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Dimension | Meaning | | Formal closure | Definitions and signatures are complete | | Computational closure | The specified operations execute | | Empirical closure | Behaviour is validated against real KnowledgeOS | | Governance closure | Required normative decisions are ratified | The implementation phase can establish at most the first two. Therefore: $$\boxed{Step\ 279 \neq Empirical\ Closure}$$ and: $$\boxed{Step\ 279 \neq Governance\ Closure}$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and applies the four-dimension closure taxonomy from Step 278 (Formal/Computational/Empirical/Governance), explicitly limiting what Step 279's implementation phase can establish to at most Formal and Computational closure; Empirical closure (validation against real KnowledgeOS) is reserved for Step 280, and Governance closure (ratified normative decisions) cannot be achieved through implementation at all. Explicitly forbids declaring 'KnowledgeOS Theory Complete' at this stage.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Governance aggregate MUST NOT directly mutate a KnowledgeState aggregate. Instead: Governance Command -> Governance Aggregate -> Governance Event -> Cross-context handler -> Knowledge/Transformation command -> Knowledge Aggregate. This preserves aggregate ownership and prevents governance from becoming a backdoor mutation mechanism.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a critical DDD invariant for the five-bounded-context implementation (Knowledge, Evidence, Assessment, Governance, History): a Governance aggregate must never directly mutate a KnowledgeState aggregate; changes must flow through a governance event and a cross-context handler that issues a proper Knowledge/Transformation command, preventing governance from becoming a backdoor mutation path.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **F1** | Policy-free transition silently receives Permit | | **F9** | Unauthorized policy mutation changes active policy | | **F13** | Declared independent rules exhibit forbidden dependency | ... These thirteen tests are the explicit computational falsification programme commissioned for Step 279.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and re-commissions the thirteen F1-F13 falsification tests (originally specified in Step 278) as the mandatory computational falsification programme for Step 279, covering policy-free/authority-free transitions, conflicting policy/authority handling, missing/expired policy detection, revoked-authority history preservation, unauthorized mutation prevention, historical-replay correctness, unsafe overlap resolution, governance-propagation convergence, and rule-independence violations. Distinguishes PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT-APPLICABLE as four distinct test-result meanings, and states explicitly PASS != Theory Proven.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 279 is CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTED. ... Required Corrections: 1. Add CombineRuleResults function ... 3. Specify calibration procedure ... 4. Add execution specifications for F1-F13 ... After corrections, Step 279 is ready for execution. ... Next: STEP 279 REVISED — EXECUTION
a_rows_sample.statement: An in-file supervisory review issues an HPA ruling of CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTED (not simply ACCEPTED) for Step 279, listing nine required corrections by severity (HIGH: calibration procedure and F1-F13 execution specs; MEDIUM: rule-combination logic, conditional-resolution-strategy operationalization, convergence conditions, aggregate commands/events, traceability test-coverage, per-scale valid operations; LOW: deny-over-permit justification), and routes the next step to 'STEP 279 REVISED — EXECUTION' rather than directly to Step 280.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The previous review shows that the previous Step 279 was conceptually correct but still too specification-oriented. ... Below is the improved, execution-ready version.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames itself explicitly as a revision responding point-by-point to the nine issues raised against the prior Step 279 draft: rule-combination semantics, executable conditional-verdict state machines, a fully specified calibration model, per-test setup/execution/pass-fail criteria for F1-F13, a measurable propagation convergence criterion, separate bounded-context testing for Policy/Authority, and a prohibition on claiming computational closure before evidence exists.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{DENY \succ CONFLICT \succ CONDITIONAL \succ UNKNOWN \succ PASS}$$ ... Combine(results): if any DENY: return DENY ... The implementation MUST test whether: $$(a\oplus b)\oplus c = a\oplus(b\oplus c)$$ for the declared composition domain. If associativity does not hold, the reason MUST be documented.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an explicit rule-combination algebra: a total precedence order DENY > CONFLICT > CONDITIONAL > UNKNOWN > PASS realized via a Combine() function, with an explicit requirement that the implementation test associativity of the combination operator over its declared domain, documenting the reason if associativity fails. This closes the gap the prior review labeled 'implicit rule-combination logic.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### WAIT ... identify event/time trigger; persist pending evaluation; schedule reassessment ### REQUEST ... ### ESCALATE ... ### REASSESS ... ### BLOCK ... terminate requested operation; return governance denial; preserve reason and evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Operationalizes the five Conditional-verdict resolution strategies as executable procedures: WAIT (persist pending evaluation, schedule reassessment on trigger), REQUEST (create request to an actor/system, await response, attach resulting evidence), ESCALATE (create escalation to higher authority, preserve original evaluation), REASSESS (wait for changed evidence/context, re-run affected rules, preserve prior assessment), BLOCK (terminate the operation, return governance denial, preserve reason and evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$Scope(o)\subseteq Scope(a)$$ and: $$Jurisdiction(o)\subseteq Jurisdiction(a).$$ If either condition fails: $$Authorize = Deny.$$ This is an executable invariant rather than a textual assumption.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies an executable Authority Scope Invariant: any Permit result requires both Scope(operation) subseteq Scope(authority) and Jurisdiction(operation) subseteq Jurisdiction(authority); if either fails, the result must be Deny. Framed explicitly as an executable check rather than a mere textual assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Calibrate(model, validation_data): generate predictions; compare predictions with observations; calculate declared calibration metric; compare metric against threshold; return: VERIFIED or FAILED ... Possible metrics include: Brier score; Expected Calibration Error; calibration slope/intercept. The implementation MUST record which metric was selected and why. A probability claim without a declared statistical model is: $$UNKNOWN.$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a concrete calibration procedure (previously flagged HIGH severity as underspecified): Calibrate(model, validation_data) generates predictions, compares them with observations, computes a declared metric (Brier score, Expected Calibration Error, or calibration slope/intercept), compares against a threshold, and returns VERIFIED or FAILED; the metric choice must be recorded and justified, and any probability claim lacking a declared statistical model is classified UNKNOWN rather than trusted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$L_i=Version(\pi_s)-Version(\pi_i).$$ Convergence occurs when: $$\forall i: L_i=0.$$ For an eventual-consistency implementation, define a finite convergence window \(\tau_c\). Then: $$\boxed{\forall i,\quad t\le t_0+\tau_c \Rightarrow Version(\pi_i)=Version(\pi_s)}$$ ... F12 passes only if convergence occurs within the declared bound. This converts "eventually reaches all nodes" into an actual executable criterion.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a measurable governance-propagation convergence criterion: version lag L_i = Version(source) - Version(node_i), with convergence requiring a finite bound tau_c such that all nodes reach the source version by t0+tau_c; F12 now passes only if convergence is observed within this declared bound, replacing the previously vague 'eventually reaches all nodes' language with an executable criterion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: # 24. F1 — Policy-Free Transition ### Setup ... ### Execute ... ### Expected $$Unknown(NoApplicablePolicy).$$ ### Pass ... ### Fail ... [through F13, each with SETUP/EXECUTE/OBSERVE/EXPECTED/PASS/FAIL]
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides fully specified, individually executable test protocols for all thirteen falsification tests F1-F13 (previously only named with an expected-yes result), each with an explicit SETUP, EXECUTE, OBSERVE, EXPECTED RESULT, PASS CONDITION, and FAIL CONDITION -- e.g. F1 (policy-free transition) requires T(K0,o) to yield exactly Unknown(NoApplicablePolicy), failing on Permit or unauthorized execution; F10 (historical replay) requires PolicyAt(t_old)=pi_1, failing if replay uses the current policy pi_2 instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{CC_{279}=ACHIEVED}$$ **only** when the above conditions are demonstrated. ... This is stronger than the previous wording and conforms to the explicit supervisory rule that computational closure may only be claimed after successful testing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Tightens the computational closure criterion to an explicit all-or-nothing conjunction: CC_279=ACHIEVED only if 15/15 components are implemented, 13/13 falsification tests are executed AND pass, traceability is established, no unresolved implementation contradiction exists, and the gap register is updated; otherwise CC_279 is PARTIAL or NOT ACHIEVED. Even if achieved, EC=ACHIEVED and GC=ACHIEVED remain unproven, and 'KnowledgeOS Theory=Complete' must not be declared.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 279 Revised is a substantially improved and execution-ready document. It has addressed all nine issues identified in the previous review ... Status: ACCEPTED — EXECUTION-READY ... Next: STEP 279 EXECUTION
a_rows_sample.statement: An in-file supervisory review issues a full ACCEPTED — EXECUTION-READY verdict for the revised Step 279 (upgraded from the prior CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTED), confirming all nine previously-identified issues are resolved (rule-combination algebra, conditional state machine, calibration, F1-F13 execution specs, propagation convergence, bounded-context separation, traceability test coverage, per-scale operations, deny-over-permit justification), and directs the process to 'STEP 279 EXECUTION' next, ahead of Step 280.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{CC\neq EC\neq GC}$$ ... Passing Step 279 does **not** imply passing Step 280.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly separates Computational Closure (CC, achieved by Step 279 -- can the specification execute) from Empirical Closure (EC, Step 280's responsibility -- does the executable theory correspond to observed real-KnowledgeOS behaviour) from Governance Closure (GC, ratification by governance authority), stating passing Step 279 does not imply passing Step 280.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{CC\neq EC\neq GC}$$ ... Passing Step 279 does **not** imply passing Step 280.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly separates Computational Closure (CC, achieved by Step 279 -- can the specification execute) from Empirical Closure (EC, Step 280's responsibility -- does the executable theory correspond to observed real-KnowledgeOS behaviour) from Governance Closure (GC, ratification by governance authority), stating passing Step 279 does not imply passing Step 280.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Case class | Minimum | ... Minimum: $$N\ge36$$ cases. ... The sample should cover: $$Context\times Operation\times EpistemicStatus\times PolicyState.$$ ... At least 20% of the empirical suite must be negative or boundary cases.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires a minimum of 36 empirical cases stratified across 12 case classes (ordinary/supported/refuted assertion, unknown/missing, contradictory, supersession, historical replay, policy-controlled, authority-controlled, policy change, conditional decision, measurement), covering the Context x Operation x EpistemicStatus x PolicyState space, with at least 20% negative/boundary cases, explicitly prohibiting demonstrating closure only on cases already known to fit the theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### Level 0 — Assertion ... ### Level 4 — Controlled empirical test ... ### Level 5 — Real KnowledgeOS validation ... ### Level 6 — Independent reproduction ... Only Levels 4–6 count as substantive empirical evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-level evidence hierarchy for empirical claims: Level 0 (bare assertion) through Level 6 (independent reproduction by another implementation/harness), explicitly ruling that only Levels 4-6 (controlled empirical test, real KnowledgeOS validation, independent reproduction) count as substantive empirical evidence -- Levels 0-3 (assertion, static correspondence, unit execution, integration execution) do not.

b_rows_sample.anchor: # 40. Critical Failure Rule The following failures automatically prevent empirical closure: 1. K cannot represent a required real state; ... 7. missingness is silently converted into a substantive value; ... 10. real KnowledgeOS behaviour requires an undefined theoretical primitive.

a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the YONI-ZERO LENS proposal in its original form on four grounds: anthropomorphic/mythological metaphor substituting for operational primitives; algebraic operators (union, Cartesian product, function composition) used interchangeably without disambiguated signatures; mixing of non-mutating queries, epistemic evaluations, and governance actions into monolithic 'Lens' operators, violating kernel-delta structural isolation; and assuming complete observability over 'Gaps'/'Unknown Gaps' without grounding in the established non-total EvalStatus vocabulary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Yoni Lens' -> Epistemic Generation Context (G_gen): An outer-kernel proposal engine that formulates candidate node assertions ASSERT(p) and link transitions LINK(p1,p2) ... 'Zero Lens' -> Epistemic Evaluation & Isolation Context (E_eval): The non-mutating analysis layer that runs EVal(K,p,Gamma), identifies partial/theory-blocked states, and triggers ISOLATE(p) when structural contradictions are detected ... 'Sarathi Lens' -> Determination Bridge Layer (Det): the decision interface mapping evaluation states, queries, and risk bounds to actionable determinations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Maps the three metaphoric 'Lenses' of the reviewed proposal onto verified Kernel v1.3 interfaces: Yoni Lens becomes an Epistemic Generation Context that proposes ASSERT/LINK candidate operations; Zero Lens becomes an Epistemic Evaluation & Isolation Context running EVal and triggering ISOLATE on detected structural contradiction; Sarathi Lens becomes the already-specified Determination Bridge Det. The three-role shape (generative proposal / boundary evaluation / decision guidance) closely parallels the corpus's earlier Zero/Lord/Sarathi guidance cycle, with the generative role renamed from 'Lord' to 'Yoni'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 1: Generative Expansion (Yoni Engine G): G(K_t,Q,Gamma) = {o_1,...,o_m} where o_i in {ASSERT,LINK,REVISE} ... Phase 2: State Mutation Transition (delta): K_temp = delta(K_t, o_m o ... o o_1, Gamma) ... Phase 3: Boundary & Partiality Examination (Zero Engine Z): Z(K_temp,Gamma) = {EVal(K_temp,p,Gamma) | p in V_temp}. If Phi_conflict(p)=true, K_{t+1}=delta(K_temp,ISOLATE(p),Gamma) ... Phase 4: Task Determination Bridge (Det): B_{t+1}=Det(Z(K_{t+1},Gamma),Q,Gamma). Cycle(K_t,Q,Gamma) = (Det o Z o delta o G)(K_t,Q,Gamma).
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the refactored four-phase epistemic cycle: Generative Expansion G produces a batch of candidate O_core operations; State Mutation delta executes them monotonically; Boundary Examination Z runs EVal over every active node and applies ISOLATE wherever the structural conflict predicate Phi_conflict holds; the Determination Bridge Det then maps the post-isolation evaluation set to a boundary/gap profile B_{t+1}. The whole cycle is the function composition Cycle(K_t,Q,Gamma) = (Det o Z o delta o G)(K_t,Q,Gamma).

VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL: Pipeline conforms to KnowledgeOS v1.3 Kernel Specification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a passing end-to-end falsification test of the refactored cycle: the Generation engine proposes two claims, one internally conflicting (high positive AND high negative support on 'A implies NOT B'); the Zero engine detects the conflict and triggers ISOLATE; the Determination bridge then correctly yields DETERMINED_POSITIVE/actionable for the clean claim and UNDETERMINED_CONFLICT/non-actionable for the isolated one, printed as 'VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL: Pipeline conforms to KnowledgeOS v1.3 Kernel Specification.'
